Core return on average tangible common equity reached 16.5%, underscoring that profitability remains solid despite a more challenging funding and rate environment.

Promotion

Record Pretax Pre-Provision Earnings and Efficiency

Pretax pre-provision earnings climbed to $36.9 million, the highest level since Equity’s three-way combination, reflecting strong core profitability. The bank kept a tight lid on operating costs, holding noninterest expense flat at $46.7 million excluding merger charges and posting an efficiency ratio of 54%, a competitive level for a regional franchise.

Organic Loan Growth in Legacy Markets

Total loans inched up $39 million to $5.44 billion, marking the first quarterly increase since the recent acquisitions closed. Growth was driven by legacy markets, where balances rose $106 million, or 2.9%, translating to nearly 12% annualized expansion and signaling renewed momentum in the core footprint.

Record Loan Production and Growing Pipeline

The bank closed a record $379 million of loans at an average rate of 6.9%, up 20% from the prior quarter and 56% year over year. Its 75% weighted loan pipeline swelled to $534 million, up 27%, while line utilization stood at 55.3%, giving management visibility into continued asset growth at attractive yields.

Expansion of Banking Teams

Equity has added 13 bankers year to date in markets including Oklahoma City, Omaha, Lincoln, Wichita and Des Moines, broadening its production capacity. These hires are still ramping, and management expects their contribution to deepen relationships and support further loan and deposit growth over time.

Improved Production in Acquired Markets

In the acquired markets, loan balances are still drifting lower, but production jumped 55% as teams adjusted to Equity’s underwriting and processes. Management views this as evidence that former targets are integrating and beginning to contribute more meaningfully, even as portfolios continue to be reshaped.

Account and Digital User Growth

Legacy markets opened 6,269 accounts in the quarter, up 22% from a year earlier, highlighting strong customer acquisition. Digital active users grew to nearly 79,000, up 10% year over year, while 759 new business accounts were added and average balances on those business accounts rose almost 4%.

Fee Income Momentum

Noninterest income rose to $10.8 million from $10.3 million on a core basis, contributing 12.9% of total revenue versus 11.2% in the prior quarter. Treasury management, card fees, trust and wealth businesses all posted gains, supporting a more diversified revenue mix at a time when spread income is under pressure.

Technology and Automation Initiatives

Management is investing in technology, automation, lead generation and enhanced services to scale more efficiently as the franchise grows. The goal is to support balance-sheet expansion without similar growth in expenses, generating positive operating leverage and improving profitability over the long term.

Lincoln Bancorp Merger Progressing

The planned merger with Lincoln Bancorp, parent of Lincoln Savings Bank, remains on track to close in the fourth quarter. The deal will add 16 locations across Central and Northeast Iowa and establish or deepen positions in Des Moines and Waterloo-Cedar Falls, taking the pro forma company to roughly $9.1 billion in assets.

Lincoln’s Strategic and Financial Contribution

Management highlighted Lincoln’s strong deposit franchise, experienced bankers and deep community ties as key strategic benefits, with no branch closures expected. The transaction is expected to deliver cost savings and earnings accretion beginning in 2027, with about half of the anticipated cost efficiencies realized during that year.

Strong Credit Metrics and Resolutions

The allowance for credit losses stood at 1.18% of loans, and classified assets to regulatory capital fell 140 basis points to 10.42% in the quarter. Executives said they remain comfortable with overall credit quality, citing successful resolutions that have helped clean up classified assets despite a modest uptick in charge-offs.

Solid Capital Generation and Dividend Increase

Capital levels remain healthy, with tangible common equity at 9.1%, CET1 at 12.15% and total risk-based capital at 14.94%. Equity generated roughly $21 million of capital during the quarter and raised its dividend by 22% to $0.22 per share, signaling confidence in its earnings power and balance-sheet strength.

Progress Toward 2026 Earnings Target

Year-to-date core earnings per share reached $4.14, putting the bank ahead of the pace needed to hit or surpass its $5 per-share goal for 2026. Management framed this as validation of the strategy to blend organic growth, cost control and selective M&A while continuing to invest in infrastructure and technology.

2027 Organic Growth Target

Looking further out, Equity sees organic loan growth of roughly 5% to 7% in 2027, calling this a mid-single-digit target. Executives added that, absent the Lincoln deal, organic growth could potentially run even stronger, underscoring the underlying momentum they see in the existing franchise.

Deposit-Gathering Opportunities

To rebuild deposits, the bank is targeting seasonal inflows from 50 to 100 municipalities whose tax revenues run through Equity accounts, particularly in the fourth quarter. Teams are also using data tools to uncover additional business held at competing banks, with an emphasis on noninterest-bearing and low-cost commercial and retail relationships.

Active but Selective M&A Strategy

Management reported four or five ongoing M&A conversations and believes the bank can handle one or two deals per year while remaining selective. Future transactions are expected to focus on markets where Equity already operates, though the company stressed it does not need more deals to stay competitive.

Infrastructure Readiness for Further Scale

Over the past three years, Equity has invested heavily in risk management, compliance and operating processes, positioning the bank for additional growth. Executives believe the company is prepared to meet heightened regulatory and operational expectations if a future deal pushes assets beyond the $10 billion threshold.

Loan Pricing Remains Accretive

New loan production carried an average yield of 6.91%, which management said remains accretive to the existing portfolio. The spot coupon on the loan book rose 8 basis points to 6.48%, and leaders expect new production and repricing to continue lifting overall loan yields even as competition intensifies.

Deposit Balance and Mix Declines

Total deposits fell $136 million, or 2.2%, to $6.17 billion, including a $102 million decline in legacy markets, reflecting ongoing funding pressures. Noninterest-bearing deposits slid to 18.7% of total deposits from 20.2% earlier in the year, prompting a renewed focus on rebuilding low-cost core funding and reducing reliance on brokered sources.

Funding Market Tightness

Management described funding markets as tight, with outflows concentrated among large, rate-sensitive customers, including public funds. Competitive pricing for deposits remains intense across both legacy and acquired markets, contributing to higher funding costs and challenging efforts to defend margin.

Declines in Acquired-Market Loan Balances

Despite better production, loan balances in acquired markets continued to decline as Equity reshapes those portfolios and runs off less attractive credits. The bank views this as a necessary near-term trade-off to improve long-term risk-adjusted returns, even if it temporarily slows reported growth.

Net Interest Income and Margin Pressure

Net interest income slipped by $1 million from the second quarter to $72.8 million, as rising funding costs outpaced asset yields. Net interest margin fell 16 basis points to 4.2%, pressured by higher deposit costs, lower yields on interest-earning assets and softer returns on investments alongside a slight dip in loan coupon yields.

Higher Deposit Costs and Borrowing-Funded Asset Growth

The total cost of deposits rose 7 basis points on essentially flat balances, while average earning assets climbed to $6.87 billion from $6.80 billion. That asset growth was funded by increased borrowings, which management said helped income but diluted margin, illustrating the trade-off between earnings and spread.

Expected Margin Impact from Lincoln

Lincoln is currently modeled to trim run-rate net interest margin by 8 to 10 basis points, reflecting its balance-sheet mix. Assuming a December 1 closing date, management expects only a modest 2 to 3 basis point margin degradation in the fourth quarter, with a greater focus on long-term earnings accretion rather than near-term spread optics.

Potential Future Margin Compression

Executives cautioned that holding or expanding margin from today’s level will be difficult as competition and funding costs remain elevated. They acknowledged that further balance-sheet growth could bring additional margin compression, even as total net interest income continues to increase with higher volumes.

Higher Net Charge-Offs and Consumer Stress

Net charge-offs rose to $2.1 million, or 15 basis points annualized, up from 12 basis points in the prior quarter, while nonperforming assets remained at 1% of total assets with $69 million in nonaccrual loans. Management also noticed some pressure in consumer deposit balances, which are down about $1,000 on average, though they said this stress has not yet translated into broader commercial credit problems.

Tangible Book Value per Share Decline

Reported tangible book value per share fell to $32.30 from $33.45, driven by a $35 million negative swing in accumulated other comprehensive income tied to higher rates. Excluding this mark-to-market impact, tangible book value per share actually rose $1.19, or about 3.6%, highlighting underlying capital generation despite rate volatility.

Share Repurchase Plan Paused

The company’s share repurchase program remains authorized but is effectively on hold while the Lincoln transaction progresses. Management cited regulatory and transaction-related constraints, along with a desire to preserve capital flexibility, as reasons for pausing buybacks in the near term.

Competitive Loan Pricing in Certain Markets

Loan pricing has become especially aggressive in select markets, forcing Equity to accept thinner spreads on some deals to remain relevant. Management characterized the level of competition in those areas as unusually intense, reinforcing the importance of relationship-based banking and disciplined underwriting.

Potential M&A Slowdown Across Smaller Banks

Rising rates and adverse accumulated other comprehensive income trends could push many smaller banks back to the sidelines, slowing industry consolidation. Equity believes some institutions missed a good window to transact over the past six months and expects fewer willing sellers near term, potentially limiting deal flow.

Guidance and Forward-Looking Outlook

For the fourth quarter, excluding Lincoln, Equity expects net interest margin to rebound into the 4.25% to 4.35% range, noninterest income between $10 million and $11 million and noninterest expense of $47 million to $48 million. The company sees quarterly provisions of roughly $1.5 million to $2 million, while the Lincoln deal is projected to close this year, create a roughly $9.1 billion pro forma bank and begin contributing earnings accretion in 2027 alongside mid-single-digit organic loan growth.

Equity Bancshares’ call painted a picture of a bank leaning into growth and technology while carefully managing funding and credit risks in a tougher rate backdrop. For investors, the story hinges on whether the company can sustain strong core profitability, successfully integrate Lincoln and execute on its 2026–2027 targets while rebuilding deposits and defending margin in a fiercely competitive market.

data.title: L&T Finance Earnings Call Signals Profitable Growth Ahead
data.description:
L&T Finance Ltd ((IN:LTF)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

L&T Finance earnings call struck a strongly upbeat tone as management celebrated record quarterly profits, robust loan growth, moderating credit costs, and stable margins. Executives acknowledged macro and rural headwinds but emphasized that technology, AI-driven risk controls, and diversified growth engines are keeping returns on an improving trajectory for shareholders.

Record profitability and improving shareholder returns

Consolidated profit after tax hit an all-time high of INR 975 crores in Q2 FY 2027, rising 33% year-on-year and signaling strong earnings momentum. Return ratios improved meaningfully, with RoA climbing to 2.60% and RoE to 13.56%, reinforcing management’s confidence in meeting near-term and Lakshya 2031 profitability goals.

Promotion

55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Rapid book expansion led by retail disbursements

The consolidated loan book expanded 28% year-on-year to INR 1,36,635 crores, driven largely by retail segments, which grew 29% to INR 1,34,600 crores. Quarterly retail disbursements rose 27% to INR 24,027 crores, with all major businesses contributing, underscoring broad-based demand and scaling distribution capabilities.

Credit costs moderating with AI-enabled collections

Credit cost eased to 2.46% in Q2 from 2.54% in Q1, supported by strong collection practices and AI-led portfolio management tools. Management reiterated its confidence in delivering a 2%-2.2% credit cost corridor by Q4 FY 2027, a key pillar for sustaining higher returns in a still uncertain macro backdrop.

Stable margins and cheaper funding support earnings

NIMs plus fees remained steady at 10.48%, comfortably within the guided 10%-10.5% band and slightly higher than last year. The weighted average cost of borrowing fell by 25 basis points thanks to active liability management, including lower-cost instruments and well-timed medium- and long-term funding.

Operating efficiency holds despite growth investments

Operating expenses stayed range-bound at 4.08% even as the company continued to roll out branches and invest in technology platforms. The cost-to-income ratio fell below 40% to roughly 39%, aided by declining collection costs as Cyclops-underwritten books show lower roll-forwards and collection bots boost productivity.

Urban finance delivers strong growth across segments

Urban finance disbursements rose 27% year-on-year to INR 10,328 crores, pushing the urban book up 32% to INR 67,668 crores. Two-wheeler loans were a standout, with disbursements up 26% and the book up 24%, and 92% of new originations in the prime segment, suggesting disciplined underwriting.

Personal loans hit record scale via partnerships

Personal loan disbursements reached a record INR 4,233 crores in the quarter, up 45% year-on-year, while the personal loan book surged 72% to INR 18,664 crores. Large partnerships contributed about 40% of originations, and integration with Airtel was operationalized, strengthening the digital distribution pipeline.

Mortgage and SME portfolios grow in targeted niches

Mortgage disbursements grew 8% year-on-year to INR 2,926 crores, lifting the mortgage book 20% to INR 32,846 crores, aided by new RM Loans for economical housing in non-metros. SME disbursements increased 24% to INR 1,820 crores, with the SME book up 27% to INR 9,495 crores, backed by risk coverage schemes.

Gold loans scale rapidly with aggressive branch rollout

Gold loan disbursements jumped 229% year-on-year to INR 3,237 crores, while the book soared 242% to INR 5,043 crores, reflecting rapid traction. The company added 172 gold branches in H1 FY 2027, reaching 502 active locations, and expects around 800 branches by year-end as it builds a nationwide footprint.

Gold loans positioned as a long-term strategic pillar

Management highlighted robust risk outcomes in gold lending, noting no loss episodes and very few auctions with strong recoveries. The company is targeting gold loan AUM at 14%-15% of overall assets, or INR 40,000-45,000 crores, by Lakshya 2031, underscoring its strategic importance in future growth.

Scaling Sampoorna multi-product branches for cross-sell

The Sampoorna network expanded to 150 branches nationwide, including 33 locations integrated with gold loans to create multi-product hubs. This model aims to convert single-product branches into full-service centers, improving cross-sell, customer engagement, and lifetime value across retail products.

Project Hercules boosts AI-led cross-sell momentum

Phase I of the agentic AI-based Hercules cross-sell engine went live across select businesses in Q2 FY 2027, showing early traction. Gold loan cross-sell leads generated from other segments are converting at over 14%, and full deployment of Hercules is expected by early December 2026.

Payments stack and UPI platform under development

The company’s UPI stack is now live in closed user group testing, forming the backbone of its future payments strategy. L&T Finance is co-building an agentic commerce and payments stack with Pine Labs and has applied for a prepaid issuer license to launch AI-enabled prepaid products from FY 2028.

Broad-based AI and technology adoption across teams

Through the AI Citizen program, over 1,200 employees now use the Google Enterprise Agent Platform, already creating 5,730 agents for daily tasks. Proprietary tools such as Cyclops, Nostradamus, and Helios are being deployed across underwriting, portfolio management, collections, and risk monitoring.

Tangible risk and collection gains from AI tools

Management cited that Nostradamus identified around INR 50 crores of potential benefit in H1 from lower collection costs and early hotspot resolution in two-wheeler and personal loans. In SME, bounce rates in Cyclops-tagged portfolios are half those of legacy books, and rural business finance collection efficiency remains near 99.8%.

Outperformance versus Lakshya 2031 growth benchmarks

Book growth of 28% in Q2 exceeded the Lakshya 2031 target of over 20% CAGR, indicating an ahead-of-plan trajectory. Long-term goals include keeping credit cost at or below 2%, raising RoA to 3%-3.2%, and RoE to 16%-18% by FY 2031, with a nearer-term RoA target of 2.8%-3% by Q4 FY 2027.

Supportive domestic demand backdrop

Management pointed to India’s robust 7.8% real GDP growth in Q1 FY 2027 and upgrades to full-year forecasts by major institutions. They described domestic demand, private consumption, investment, exports, services, employment, and manufacturing activity as resilient, underpinning credit demand.

Risk mitigation via insurance and guarantee schemes

The company is actively using CGFMU and CGTMSE guarantee schemes and parametric insurance to lower portfolio risks and capital needs. Around 80% of the SME book is covered under CGTMSE, and parametric insurance yielded meaningful recoveries from recent flooding in Bihar, cushioning rural stress.

Macro and geopolitical uncertainties cloud outlook

Management flagged renewed conflict in West Asia, volatile crude prices, persistent inflation, and expectations of higher-for-longer policy rates as key risks. Elevated input costs and limited pass-through so far add pressure, which the company is trying to offset through pricing discipline and efficiency.

Weak monsoon raises rural and farm risks

The 2026 southwest monsoon ended at about 87% of the long-period average, with significant regional shortfalls that could hit farm output and rural incomes. Management is closely monitoring drought-prone areas and recognizes localized crop-yield declines and softer rural sentiment as emerging risk factors.

Muted rural and farm disbursements amid caution

Rural business finance disbursements grew just 1% year-on-year to INR 6,356 crores, and farm finance disbursements fell 1% to INR 1,643 crores as risk guardrails were tightened. Management said customer demand was subdued in affected regions and indicated a deliberate moderation to avoid future stress.

Potential impact from proposed IRDAI commission changes

A draft IRDAI consultation paper proposes significant cuts to credit-linked and motor insurance commissions and new thresholds for standalone products. While the final outcome remains uncertain, management acknowledged that business models may need to evolve and is preparing alternative revenue levers.

Expected rise in interest rates and funding costs

Executives expect further increases in policy rates, with incremental borrowing yields already up 30-50 basis points across instruments. Despite this, they believe NIMs plus fees can stay within the 10%-10.5% range given pricing actions and funding strategies, though investors should watch this closely.

Two-wheeler collection hiccup from AI experiment

Two-wheeler collection efficiency slipped in September after an aggressive experiment to lift AI-driven self-cure rates from around 43% to above 50%. The initiative did not deliver as planned, but management reported that collection efficiency has normalized to roughly 99% or slightly better in October.

Sequentially flat personal loans amid Cyclops rollout

Personal loan disbursements were broadly flat quarter-on-quarter as the company rolled out Cyclops partner by partner, including one over-correction that temporarily curbed volumes. One large partner is still to be integrated, and new partnerships now take three to four months to fully ramp under stricter risk controls.

Lower fee income due to liquidity and product mix

Fee and other income fell by about 20-22 basis points versus Q1 FY 2027, reflecting the absence of earnings from INR 4,000 crores of excess liquidity held earlier. Management added that fee flows fluctuate with product mix and noted that insurance has not yet been activated on gold loan disbursements.

Uncertain but manageable outlook for rural crops

The outlook for the rabi crop is still uncertain after a weak monsoon, but management expects near-normal outcomes based on field feedback and reservoir levels. Retreating monsoon patterns and government measures are supporting sentiment, and the company is cautiously optimistic on rural cash flow stabilization.

Forward-looking guidance and growth trajectory

Management reaffirmed a credit cost corridor of 2%-2.2%, NIMs plus fees of 10%-10.5%, and RoA of 2.8%-3% by Q4 FY 2027, aligned with Lakshya 2031 goals of 20%+ book CAGR, sub-2% credit costs, and RoE of 16%-18%. Rural disbursements are expected to pick up modestly, personal loans to scale to an interim INR 1,700-1,800 crores monthly, and gold branches to reach around 800 this year as AI-enabled payments products are targeted for FY 2028.

L&T Finance’s latest earnings call painted a picture of a lender balancing strong growth and profitability with prudent risk management in a challenging macro environment. For investors, the key takeaways are record earnings, rapid retail and gold loan expansion, deepening AI capabilities, and clear long-term return targets, tempered by rural, regulatory, and rate-related uncertainties.

data.title: CTW Cayman Class A Maps Path to 2027 Growth
data.description:
CTW Cayman Class A ((CTW)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

CTW Cayman Class A’s latest earnings call struck a cautious but constructive tone. Management acknowledged weaker revenue, user metrics and profitability, yet highlighted disciplined advertising, stronger segment margins, a debt-free balance sheet and growing international diversification. The company framed fiscal 2026 as a transition year and pointed firmly to a long-term plan to restore sustainable growth by fiscal 2027.

Advertising Efficiency Holds Above Benchmark

Return on advertising spend was 105.8% in fiscal 2026, down from 116.4% a year earlier but still above CTW’s 100% threshold. This means in-game purchases from newly acquired users continued to exceed the cost of acquiring them, underscoring a disciplined approach to marketing even as the company tightened spending.

Promotion

55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Segment Profit Rises Despite Revenue Decline

Segment profit climbed 3% to $32.3 million, representing 33.4% of in-game purchases versus 29.3% last year. Lower advertising expenses more than offset reduced in-game purchases and higher server costs, indicating CTW can preserve profitability in its core operations even in a softer demand environment.

Positive Adjusted EBITDA and Clean Balance Sheet

Adjusted EBITDA remained in the black at $3.5 million, equal to 4.2% of revenue, though it was down from the prior year. CTW ended fiscal 2026 with $14.4 million in cash and cash equivalents and no debt, giving the company financial flexibility to invest in content and technology while weathering near-term volatility.

New Titles and High School of the Dead Momentum

CTW launched 15 new games during the year, finishing with 42 active titles across its platform. High School of the Dead: Day 0 stood out, generating about $6 million in a little over three months and ranking as the platform’s top revenue contributor over that period, offering proof that the right IP can still deliver strong traction.

Paying User Metrics Show Improvement

Paying monthly active users edged up to roughly 89,100 from about 88,500, bucking broader declines in total users. The conversion ratio of paying users to total monthly active users improved meaningfully to 3.95% from 2.62%, suggesting CTW is becoming more effective at monetizing engaged players even as casual traffic falls.

International Revenue Mix Broadens

Revenue from users outside Japan rose 8.2% to $29.7 million, and now accounts for 36% of total revenue versus 30.4% a year ago. South Korea revenue increased 12.4% to $10.5 million, while Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau collectively surged 71.2% to $8 million, reflecting progress in diversifying away from the home market.

Regional Momentum Across Asia

Combined revenue from South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau grew 31.9% to $18.5 million, representing 22.4% of total revenue, up from 15.5%. Management highlighted strong anime appeal across these markets, viewing the region as a key growth engine that can offset softness in more mature territories.

Advertising Cuts Tied to Performance Hurdles

Sales and marketing spending fell 17.2% to $45.9 million, led by a 21.7% reduction in advertising to $41 million. Executives stressed that the pullback was deliberate, as CTW scaled down marketing for titles that failed to meet internal performance thresholds, reinforcing a data-driven approach to user acquisition.

Public Company Infrastructure Now Built Out

General and administrative expenses increased as CTW expanded its corporate functions and opened a New York City office. Management said the core public company infrastructure is largely in place, and expects G&A to grow only modestly in absolute terms over time, allowing operating leverage as revenue scales.

Liquidity Underpinned by IPO Proceeds

The company’s $14.4 million cash balance at year-end was up from $12.2 million in the prior fiscal year. This included $10.6 million of net proceeds from its IPO, providing liquidity to support selective investment in new content, systems and international expansion despite recent operating cash outflows.

Anime and Manga IP Portfolio Remains Broad

CTW ended fiscal 2026 with partnerships spanning 38 anime IP holders and 48 IP licenses. Management argued that commercial potential is not solely tied to recent hits, and plans to keep a diversified mix of well-known anime, catalog IPs, original games and multiple genres to balance risk across titles.

Browser Platform Offers Alternative Distribution

The G123 platform operates via browser and is accessible globally without app downloads, sidestepping traditional app store constraints. In-game purchases run through third-party payment providers directly connected to the platform, a model CTW believes will benefit from rising developer interest in non-app-store channels.

North American Business Development Efforts Expand

CTW’s New York team, formed in early 2026, is focused on partnerships, localization and user acquisition in North America. Participation in major anime events helped the company engage with licensing and gaming professionals, laying groundwork for future titles and marketing campaigns in the region.

Ongoing Platform and Technology Investment

CTW capitalized $4.1 million of internal-use software development for its G123 platform under new accounting rules. The software supports game launches, marketing, localization and operations, helping the company handle a larger slate of titles and higher user volumes without proportionally increasing headcount.

Pursuing Efficiency and New Marketing Channels

Management plans to keep investing in platform and internal technology, including AI-enabled tools, analytics and workflow automation. The company is also reviewing distribution and marketing partnerships, collaborations with local content creators and influencers, and additional user acquisition channels to improve efficiency.

Disciplined Advances and Content Funding

CTW views advances to game developers as central to its model and assesses IP strength, developer skill and past results before committing capital. The company invested $6 million in such advances in fiscal 2026 to secure future content, while acknowledging that performance risk cannot be fully eliminated.

Revenue and In-Game Purchases Under Pressure

Fiscal 2026 revenue fell 8.7% to $82.5 million, while gross in-game purchases dropped 9.5% to $96.8 million. Management linked the declines to weaker game launches and aging titles, signaling that fresh, successful content remains essential to reversing the top-line trend.

Underperforming Launches and Aging Catalog

Games released in the first half of the year underperformed expectations, while several older titles moved further into late-life cycles. These factors weighed on user engagement and monetization, contributing to the drop in in-game purchases and highlighting the importance of a more consistent launch slate.

Monthly Active Users See Steep Decline

Total monthly active users fell 33% to about 2.26 million from roughly 3.38 million. Management said the decline was concentrated among non-paying users, partially mitigating revenue impact but underscoring the need to reinvigorate the broader audience base.

Daily Paying Users and ARPPU Slip

Paying daily active users declined 13%, exceeding the 7% drop in overall daily active users. Average revenue per paying monthly active user slid to $90.60 from $100.74, indicating that not only are fewer players paying frequently, but spend per paying user is also softening.

ROAS and Adjusted EBITDA Trend Lower

While ROAS remained above the company benchmark, it declined from 116.4% to 105.8% year over year. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $3.5 million, or 4.2% of revenue, from $8 million, or 8.8%, showing that profitability has compressed as content and cost pressures intensified.

Japan and North America Revenue Weakness

North American revenue dropped to $6.2 million from $7.5 million as CTW reduced user acquisition spending on underperforming games. Japan, still the largest market, saw revenue decline 16.1% to $52.8 million, reinforcing management’s push to accelerate growth in other regions.

Rising Costs Erode Margins

Cost of revenue rose 29.2% to $28.5 million, driven by higher personnel, outsourcing, server, software and IP revenue share costs, plus amortization. General and administrative expenses increased 37.9% to $11.7 million, including Taiwan business taxes, pressuring margins despite lower marketing spend.

Operating Loss and Net Results Worsen

CTW posted an operating loss of $7.3 million, widening from a $1.1 million loss a year earlier. Net results swung to a $4.1 million loss, or $0.07 per share, compared with net income of $3.8 million, or $0.06 per share, underscoring the financial impact of weaker launches and higher costs.

Higher Operating and Investing Cash Outflows

Net cash used in operating activities was $3.2 million, compared with a small cash inflow in the prior year. Investing cash outflows reached $4.7 million, largely due to $4.1 million of capitalized software development, reflecting CTW’s bet on future platform capabilities at the expense of near-term free cash flow.

Ongoing Impairments on Developer Advances

CTW recorded about $2.6 million of impairments on advances to game developers, slightly below the prior year’s level. Management reiterated that predicting actual game performance is inherently challenging and that no evaluation process can fully remove the risk of unsuccessful launches.

Preregistration Not a Guaranteed Success Metric

Executives cautioned that strong preregistration figures mainly boost awareness and early user acquisition efficiency. They do not guarantee high retention or better conversion to paying users post-launch, prompting CTW to rely on broader performance indicators when assessing game potential.

Future Amortization from Capitalized Software

Of the $4.1 million in capitalized software, about $3.5 million remained net after amortization, with roughly $2.5 million already in service and $1 million under development. Management expects around $1 million in annual amortization over each of the next two fiscal years, adding a predictable non-cash expense to the P&L.

Forward Outlook and Strategic Priorities

CTW laid out a vision to return to sustained growth in fiscal 2027, with expectations that North American revenue will resume growth as new titles launch and regional initiatives take hold. The company plans modest G&A increases, continued investment in AI-enabled tools, data analytics and workflow automation, and warned that near-term movements in monthly active users and in-game purchases may diverge.

CTW’s earnings call painted a picture of a company balancing near-term headwinds with strategic investment and geographic diversification. Investors will watch whether improved monetization, new titles and technology upgrades can offset declining legacy games and rising costs, and whether management’s 2027 growth vision translates into tangible recovery in revenue and profitability.

Surging Earnings Per Share

Earnings per share climbed to INR 22.26, marking growth of 44.34% versus a year earlier and 16.25% over the previous quarter. Management framed this EPS trajectory as validation of the bank’s improving profitability and capital efficiency.

Scaling Up the Balance Sheet

The bank crossed key scale milestones as total business exceeded INR 6 lakh crore and gross advances topped INR 3 lakh crore. These thresholds signal Federal Bank’s progression into a larger league within India’s banking system.

Net Interest Income and Margin Resilience

Net interest income rose to INR 3,153.4 crore, up 26.38% year-on-year and 7% quarter-on-quarter, supported by healthy loan growth and pricing discipline. The net interest margin held at 3.32%, only 1 basis point lower sequentially and 26 basis points higher than a year ago, with management reiterating an expectation of gradual margin improvement.

Deposits and CASA Franchise Strengthening

Total deposits reached INR 304,269 crore, showing 18.6% annual growth and 7% sequential expansion. Low-cost CASA balances grew faster than overall deposits, rising 22.56% year-on-year to INR 109,803 crore, helping lift the CASA ratio by 103 basis points and pushing average CASA above the INR 1 lakh crore mark.

Robust NRI and Demand Deposit Flows

NRE and NRO deposits together climbed to INR 119,055 crore, up 26.6% year-on-year and 13.25% quarter-on-quarter. Savings balances rose nearly 4% sequentially and 19.6% annually, while demand deposits jumped 33% year-on-year, extending a roughly six-quarter run of strong CASA traction.

Disciplined Loan Growth in Focused Segments

Gross advances stood at INR 301,687 crore, growing 21% year-on-year and 7.27% quarter-on-quarter. Management reiterated mid-teens loan growth guidance and stressed a focus on granular, high-yielding assets designed to enhance risk-adjusted returns rather than sheer volume.

Broad-Based Expansion Across Product Lines

Growth was spread across segments, with gold loans up 37.13% year-on-year and 6.67% sequentially and LAP rising 32.21% annually. Credit cards, commercial banking, CV/CE, corporate and institutional banking, business banking and retail banking all posted double-digit increases, underscoring diversified momentum.

Record Fee and Other Income

Fee income reached INR 1,167 crore, up 31.86% year-on-year and 22% quarter-on-quarter, taking fee income relative to assets to a record 1.11%. Total other income was INR 1,490 crore, the highest in the bank’s history, with management noting broad-based contributions across fee-generating businesses.

Improving Efficiency and Cost Discipline

The cost-to-income ratio improved to 52%, dropping 196 basis points versus last year and 42 basis points quarterly. Management signaled an intent to operate roughly around this level and emphasized keeping revenue growth structurally ahead of cost growth.

Asset Quality at Decadal Lows

Gross non-performing assets fell to 1.32%, down 20 basis points sequentially and 51 basis points year-on-year. Net NPA dropped to 0.17%, which management described as best-in-class, marking the lowest levels seen in about a decade.

Lower Credit Costs and Strong Coverage

Credit cost declined to 0.31%, improving by 10 basis points quarter-on-quarter and 19 basis points year-on-year. Provision coverage reached 86.78% excluding technical write-offs and 94.4% including them, with coverage improving by 1,300 basis points over the year.

Returns and Capital Buffers Strengthen

Return on assets improved to about 1.32%–1.33%, up 10 basis points sequentially and 23 basis points versus last year. Return on equity rose to 13.57%, while book value per share climbed to INR 166.32 and the capital adequacy ratio stood at a comfortable 16.84%.

FCNR(B) Strategy and Liability Management

The bank secured a meaningful share of FCNR(B) deposits under the special window, with management describing the size, economics and tenors as well suited to its balance sheet and asset-liability profile. This move reflects a deliberate strategy to diversify and optimize liabilities.

Investing in Technology and Distribution

Management said the bank is stepping up investments in technology, new branches, a fresh sales channel, additional staffing and related initiatives. Strengthening digital and AI capabilities is a stated priority to position the franchise competitively for the next phase of growth.

Strategic Emphasis on NRI and Wealth

The bank reaffirmed its commitment to its NRI franchise, aiming to serve clients more holistically. Building out the wealth management business is a key part of that strategy, targeting deeper relationships and higher fee-based income.

Conservative Approach to Inorganic Growth

On acquisitions, management emphasized that any deal must be earnings-accretive and complement its universal banking model. It favors a “string of pearls” approach, adding selective capabilities or scale, rather than pursuing a single transformational transaction.

Gold Loan Product and Pricing Actions

Federal Bank highlighted that gold loans, typically one-year in tenor, can be repriced as rates move, allowing yield optimization. It launched income-generating gold loans in the quarter under a new policy, a product that offers slightly higher yields and supports margin enhancement.

Board and Leadership Reinforcements

Virat Diwanji, formerly National Head of Consumer Banking, joined the board, adding retail expertise. The bank also welcomed independent director Rajesh Varrier, whose technology background is seen as valuable for guiding the institution’s digital and AI agenda.

Macro Backdrop: Inflation and Policy Tightening

Management reviewed a more challenging macro backdrop, with headline CPI averaging about 4.94% in the quarter and remaining above the central bank’s 4% target for four months. The policy rate was raised by 25 basis points to 5.5%, alongside a shift to calibrated tightening and a higher medium-term inflation projection.

Moderation in Deposit Cost Tailwinds

The benefit from falling deposit costs began to moderate, with the cost of deposits declining only 3 basis points quarter-on-quarter versus a 22-basis-point drop previously. Management cautioned that competition for deposits is likely to intensify as liquidity conditions normalize.

FCNR Deposits’ Impact on Reported NIM

Management acknowledged that FCNR-related leverage affected the reported NIM of 3.32%. They indicated that margins would have printed higher without this impact, while noting the exact effect varies with the assumptions used in analysis.

One-Time ESOP Accounting Change

From April 1, 2026, the bank shifted to fair value accounting for employee stock options, leading to incremental employee costs of INR 32.7 crore and a PAT impact of INR 24.5 crore. Management described the INR 32 crore effect as a one-time adjustment linked to the accounting transition.

Operating Expenses Reflect Growth Investments

Operating costs were elevated by spending on new branches, staff additions, a fresh sales channel, technology upgrades and actuarial impacts. Retirement-related provisions may be written back in coming quarters as interest rate movements reverse some of the earlier actuarial charges.

Treasury Gains Seen as Non-Recurring

Treasury income was boosted by gains on encashed investments, IPO-related benefits and other encashments, as well as a rebound from unusually weak income in the previous two quarters. Management cautioned that this was a particularly strong treasury quarter and may not be repeated at the same level.

Regulatory Overhang on Bancassurance Fees

The bank acknowledged that draft rules could affect bancassurance fee income, which totaled about INR 390 crore in the prior year. With the final contours yet to be clarified, management plans to assess the potential impact over the coming quarter.

External Risks Closely Monitored

Management said it is monitoring risks from El Niño, geopolitics, interest rates and inflation, and has taken a cautious stance in segments like agriculture and microfinance. It noted that, so far, these external factors have not materially affected asset quality.

Non-Linear Growth and Margin Trajectories

While reiterating mid-teens growth and gradual NIM improvement guidance, management emphasized that quarterly outcomes will not be linear. Investors were advised to focus on full-year trends rather than expecting smooth quarter-on-quarter progression.

ECL Transition Impact Well Contained

The bank reiterated that the impact from transitioning to expected credit loss norms is less than 2% of net worth. Importantly, this estimate remains unchanged despite a recent 40-basis-point rise in bond yields.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Outlook

Management maintained guidance for mid-teens growth, average NIM improvement of 5–6 basis points per quarter and ROA gains of 3–4 basis points per quarter over the year. CASA targets remain intact, cost-to-income is expected to hover around the low-50s and the liquidity coverage ratio is aimed within a 110%–120% band, underscoring a balanced growth-risk posture.

Federal Bank’s earnings call painted a picture of a franchise in strong health, combining record profits, wider margins and cleaner books with continued investment in future capabilities. While the bank acknowledged macro, regulatory and funding headwinds, management’s steady guidance and emphasis on disciplined growth suggest that it sees ample runway for sustainable performance.
